ai.title: transformMessages handles Message in ai-sdk
ai.summary: Exported transformMessages in backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts now accepts (GeminiMessage | Message)[]. Added explicit handling for Message image sources, text parts, and assistant tool_use blocks while skipping user tool parts. This broadens input compatibility for the Vercel AI SDK adapter.

eli5.text: The tool that converts incoming messages for the AI now accepts a second type of message format, so you can send image and tool-call data without it being rejected. Internally, the message converter (transformMessages) now accepts both GeminiMessage and Message types instead of just one. New handling covers Message-type image sources, text parts, and assistant tool_use blocks, while user tool parts are skipped. This is a backend change, so you won't notice anything on the surface, but it allows the AI to process these messages more reliably.

ai.title: Remove cache-invalidating filter in main-prompt
ai.summary: Removed `isSystemInstruction` filter from `messageHistory` processing in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. This change ensures all messages are mapped via `castAssistantMessage` regardless of system instruction status, stabilizing the prompt structure for caching. Internal refactor affecting backend prompt assembly logic. No user-facing behavior change expected beyond improved cache consistency.

eli5.text: The conversation history is no longer filtered to exclude system instructions, so all messages are processed the same way by the backend. This is an internal adjustment to how prompts are assembled and cached, with no visible change to how the assistant behaves. It went live today.

ai.title: Fix processStrReplace line ending normalization
ai.summary: `processStrReplace` now normalizes newline characters within extracted diff hunks using `replaceAll`. This ensures consistent line endings when constructing patch strings from raw diff content. The change applies to `backend/src/process-str-replace.ts` and its corresponding unit test.

eli5.text: When the system builds a text patch from raw diff content, it now converts all line breaks in the extracted section to match the surrounding line-ending style before saving it. Previously, mismatched newlines could slip through, but now they are normalized consistently at the point where a patch hunk is captured, so the constructed patch stays coherent end to end.

ai.title: Fix usage calculation tests
ai.summary: Corrected mock paths and return types in usage-calculation.test.ts. Updated logger mock to common/util/logger and made orderBy return a Promise. Added test for in-memory settlement between positive balance and debt.

eli5.text: The system now correctly accounts for a user's account balance when they have both money owed to them and money they owe. For example, if your account has $100 in credit and $50 in debt, the system properly nets those against each other to show a final balance of $50. This fixes a bug where the balance calculation could show incorrect totals, which may have affected how usage was tracked on your account. The correction is in place and applies to accounts where settlement between positive and negative balances is needed.

ai.title: Add automatic client-side exception capture
ai.summary: Added `logError` to `common/src/analytics.ts` and `npm-app/src/utils/analytics.ts` to wrap PostHog's `captureException`. `npm-app/src/utils/logger.ts` now intercepts `error` and `fatal` pino logs, converting them into analytics exceptions via `logAsErrorIfNeeded`. `npm-app/src/client.ts` and `npm-app/src/update-codebuff.ts` replace manual `trackEvent` error reporting with structured `logger.error` calls. PostHog client initialization in `npm-app/src/utils/analytics.ts` enables `enableExceptionAutocapture`.

eli5.text: When something goes wrong while you're using CodeBuff, those errors are now automatically captured and sent to the analytics system without requiring manual reporting. The application now intercepts error-level log messages and converts them into structured error reports, so previously manual error tracking calls have been replaced with standardized logging calls that automatically include relevant details like error messages, status codes, and stack traces. Who it affects: Anyone using CodeBuff when errors occur, they'll benefit from more reliable crash reporting without any action needed on their part. What you'd notice: Errors are now consistently tracked across the application with structured details, rather than being reported sporadically or through console messages.

ai.title: Add /reset command to clear conversation context
ai.summary: The /reset command clears conversation state, terminates background processes, and reinitializes the project context as if starting a new session. This requires refactoring `currentChatId` from a static export to a mutable variable managed by `getCurrentChatId` and `startNewChat` functions in `project-files.ts`. The `Client.resetContext` method orchestrates the clearing of messages, checkpoints, and tool results, while `cli.ts` handles the terminal clearing and process restart logic.

eli5.text: When you type /reset during a conversation with the assistant, it wipes the current chat clean and starts fresh, like closing one browser tab and opening a brand new one. This affects anyone using the assistant directly in the terminal: you lose your conversation history, any files it was tracking get a fresh look at your project, and the screen clears to a clean state. Looking behind the scenes, the change adds a new /reset command to the assistant's menu and rewrites how it tracks which chat session you're in, so instead of a single fixed identifier it creates a new one each time you reset. This is live today: the command works the moment you type /reset, and the evidence shows it shipped alongside code that clears stored messages, resets background tasks, and reloads your project

ai.title: Track git repo metrics in analytics
ai.summary: Added getRepoMetrics utility to extract git repository statistics (age, tracked files, commits, authors) using isomorphic-git. These metrics are attached to PostHog user profiles and logger context during client initialization. The repoName field was propagated through backend prompt actions and file request functions to support analytics tagging.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant today, it quietly reads your git repository (the project you are working on) and records stats like how old the project is, how many files it tracks, and how many people have contributed, attaching those details to your usage profile for internal analytics. The repository name also travels with your requests through the backend so the metrics can be correctly tagged per project. If you looked at the change, you would see the new reporting shows up only in logs and internal analytics tools, not in any new feature or menu you can open.

ai.title: Refactor LLM streaming to unified AI SDK approach
ai.summary: Refactored LLM streaming in `backend/src/prompt-agent-stream.ts` to use `promptAiSdkStream` from `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts`, replacing direct provider-specific calls (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter). Added `stopSequences` support to `promptAiSdkStream` and `promptAiSdk` signatures. Removed imports for `models`, `OpenAIModel`, `openrouterModels`, and provider-specific stream functions. Consolidated message transformation via `transformMessages`.

eli5.text: The way the app talks to different AI providers was consolidated behind one common interface, so adding or swapping models no longer requires provider-specific wiring at each call site. If you maintain or extend this code path, you now pass stop sequences directly to the unified entry point and rely on a single message-transform step instead of per-provider stream functions; nothing else observable changes for end users today.
